/-!
# Conjecture 2.78

by P. I. Trofimov

Any set of all subgroups of the same given order of a finite group $G$ that contains at
least one non-normal subgroup is called an $IE_{\bar n}$-system of $G$. A positive integer
$k$ is called a *soluble* (*non-soluble*; *simple*; *composite*; *absolutely simple*)
*group-theoretic number* if every finite group having exactly $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems is
soluble (respectively, if there is at least one non-soluble finite group having $k$
$IE_{\bar n}$-systems; if there is at least one simple finite group having $k$
$IE_{\bar n}$-systems; if there are no simple finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems;
if there is at least one simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems and there are
no non-soluble non-simple finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems).

Are the sets of all soluble and of all absolutely simple group-theoretic numbers finite or
infinite? Do there exist composite, but not soluble group-theoretic numbers?

The predicates `IsSolubleNumber`, `IsNonSolubleNumber`, `IsSimpleNumber`, `IsCompositeNumber`
and `IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber` below are defined for every natural number $k$; the restriction
to positive $k$ is imposed in the problem statements.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.ncard / Nat.card directly on {d | ∃ H, ¬H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d}; chose the literal 'count the systems' definition and proved equivalence to the order-count.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.78».numIESystems

blocks.name: numIESystems
blocks.text:
/-- The number of $IE_{\bar n}$-systems of a group $G$. For a finite group $G$ this is the
number of orders $d$ such that $G$ has a non-normal subgroup of order $d$. -/
noncomputable def numIESystems (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ :=
  {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S}.ncard

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem numIESystems_eq_ncard (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    numIESystems G = {d : ℕ | ∃ H : Subgroup G, ¬ H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d}.ncard := by
  have himage : {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S} =
      (fun d : ℕ => {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d}) ''
        {d : ℕ | ∃ H : Subgroup G, ¬ H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d} := by
    ext S
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, H, hHd, hH⟩
      exact ⟨d, ⟨H, hH, hHd⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨d, ⟨H, hH, hHd⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, H, hHd, hH⟩
  rw [numIESystems, himage, Set.ncard_image_of_injOn]
  rintro d ⟨H, -, hHd⟩ d' - h
  have : H ∈ {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d'} := by
    rw [← show {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d} = {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d'} from h]
    exact hHd
  exact hHd.symm.trans this
blocks.docstring:
The number of $IE_{\bar n}$-systems of $G$ is the number of orders $d$ such that $G$ has a
non-normal subgroup of order $d$.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem numIESystems_eq_ncard (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    numIESystems G = {d : ℕ | ∃ H : Subgroup G, ¬ H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d}.ncard := by
  have himage : {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S} =
      (fun d : ℕ => {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d}) ''
        {d : ℕ | ∃ H : Subgroup G, ¬ H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d} := by
    ext S
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, H, hHd, hH⟩
      exact ⟨d, ⟨H, hH, hHd⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨d, ⟨H, hH, hHd⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, H, hHd, hH⟩
  rw [numIESystems, himage, Set.ncard_image_of_injOn]
  rintro d ⟨H, -, hHd⟩ d' - h
  have : H ∈ {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d'} := by
    rw [← show {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d} = {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d'} from h]

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem numIESystems_eq_zero_of_forall_normal (h : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Normal) :
    numIESystems G = 0 := by
  have : {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S} = ∅ := by
    rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    rintro S ⟨-, H, -, hH⟩
    exact hH (h H)
  rw [numIESystems, this, Set.ncard_empty]
blocks.docstring: A group in which every subgroup is normal has no $IE_{\bar n}$-systems.
blocks.name: numIESystems_eq_zero_of_forall_normal
blocks.text:
/-- A group in which every subgroup is normal has no $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem numIESystems_eq_zero_of_forall_normal (h : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Normal) :
    numIESystems G = 0 := by
  have : {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S} = ∅ := by
    rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    rintro S ⟨-, H, -, hH⟩
    exact hH (h H)
  rw [numIESystems, this, Set.ncard_empty]

  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], numIESystems G = k → IsSolvable G

finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/

blocks.docstring:
A positive integer $k$ is an *absolutely simple group-theoretic number* if there is at
least one simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems and there are no non-soluble

justification.name: Kourovka.«2.78».IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber

blocks.name: IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber
blocks.text:
/-- A positive integer $k$ is an *absolutely simple group-theoretic number* if there is at
least one simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems and there are no non-soluble
non-simple finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
def IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsSimpleNumber k ∧
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], numIESystems G = k → ¬ IsSolvable G → IsSimpleGroup G

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNonSolubleNumber_iff_not_isSolubleNumber (k : ℕ) :
    IsNonSolubleNumber k ↔ ¬ IsSolubleNumber k := by
  simp only [IsNonSolubleNumber, IsSolubleNumber, not_forall, exists_prop]
blocks.docstring:
A positive integer $k$ is a non-soluble group-theoretic number if and only if it is not a
soluble group-theoretic number.
blocks.name: isNonSolubleNumber_iff_not_isSolubleNumber

soluble group-theoretic number. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNonSolubleNumber_iff_not_isSolubleNumber (k : ℕ) :
    IsNonSolubleNumber k ↔ ¬ IsSolubleNumber k := by
  simp only [IsNonSolubleNumber, IsSolubleNumber, not_forall, exists_prop]

claims.decomposer_note: First half of the compound question: is the set {k ≥ 1 | every finite group with exactly k IE_n̄-systems is soluble} finite? — 'finite or infinite' is a dichotomy so the Prop is Set.Finite of that set (answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite …); the number of IE_n̄-systems of G is the number of orders d such that G has at least one non-normal subgroup of order d, and k ranges over positive integers only (k = 0 excluded, though Dedekind groups are soluble anyway).
claims.reviewer_why: answer(sorry) ↔ {k | 0 < k ∧ IsSolubleNumber k}.Finite with IsSolubleNumber k := ∀ finite G, numIESystems G = k → IsSolvable G. Matches 'every finite group having exactly k IE-systems is soluble', k positive. numIESystems is the literal count of sets-of-all-subgroups-of-an-order containing a non-normal subgroup (Set.ncard on a finite ambient type for finite G), with a proved API lemma showing it equals the number of orders admitting a non-normal subgroup. All eight candidates were mathematically equivalent here; c01 chosen for the literal definition plus proved bridging lemma, slot-matching theorem names, and clean compile. Docstring edited to make the True=finite / False=infinite reading explicit.

/-!

Are the sets of all soluble and of all absolutely simple group-theoretic numbers finite or
infinite? Do there exist composite, but not soluble group-theoretic numbers?

The predicates `IsSolubleNumber`, `IsNonSolubleNumber`, `IsSimpleNumber`, `IsCompositeNumber`
and `IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber` below are defined for every natural number $k$; the restriction
to positive $k$ is imposed in the problem statements.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«2.78»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A set $S$ of subgroups of a group $G$ is an $IE_{\bar n}$-system of $G$ if $S$ is the set
of all subgroups of $G$ of some given order $d$, and $S$ contains at least one non-normal
subgroup. -/
def IsIESystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  (∃ d : ℕ, S = {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d}) ∧ ∃ H ∈ S, ¬ H.Normal

/-- The number of $IE_{\bar n}$-systems of a group $G$. For a finite group $G$ this is the
number of orders $d$ such that $G$ has a non-normal subgroup of order $d$. -/
noncomputable def numIESystems (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ :=
  {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S}.ncard

/-- The number of $IE_{\bar n}$-systems of $G$ is the number of orders $d$ such that $G$ has a
non-normal subgroup of order $d$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem numIESystems_eq_ncard (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    numIESystems G = {d : ℕ | ∃ H : Subgroup G, ¬ H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d}.ncard := by
  have himage : {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S} =
      (fun d : ℕ => {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d}) ''
        {d : ℕ | ∃ H : Subgroup G, ¬ H.Normal ∧ Nat.card H = d} := by
    ext S
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, H, hHd, hH⟩
      exact ⟨d, ⟨H, hH, hHd⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨d, ⟨H, hH, hHd⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, H, hHd, hH⟩
  rw [numIESystems, himage, Set.ncard_image_of_injOn]
  rintro d ⟨H, -, hHd⟩ d' - h
  have : H ∈ {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d'} := by
    rw [← show {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d} = {H : Subgroup G | Nat.card H = d'} from h]
    exact hHd
  exact hHd.symm.trans this

/-- A group in which every subgroup is normal has no $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem numIESystems_eq_zero_of_forall_normal (h : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Normal) :
    numIESystems G = 0 := by
  have : {S : Set (Subgroup G) | IsIESystem S} = ∅ := by
    rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    rintro S ⟨-, H, -, hH⟩
    exact hH (h H)
  rw [numIESystems, this, Set.ncard_empty]

/-- A positive integer $k$ is a *soluble group-theoretic number* if every finite group having
exactly $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems is soluble. -/
def IsSolubleNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], numIESystems G = k → IsSolvable G

/-- A positive integer $k$ is a *non-soluble group-theoretic number* if there is at least one
non-soluble finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
def IsNonSolubleNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), numIESystems G = k ∧ ¬ IsSolvable G

/-- A positive integer $k$ is a *simple group-theoretic number* if there is at least one
simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
def IsSimpleNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G), numIESystems G = k ∧ IsSimpleGroup G

/-- A positive integer $k$ is a *composite group-theoretic number* if there are no simple
finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
def IsCompositeNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], numIESystems G = k → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G

/-- A positive integer $k$ is an *absolutely simple group-theoretic number* if there is at
least one simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems and there are no non-soluble
non-simple finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems. -/
def IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsSimpleNumber k ∧
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], numIESystems G = k → ¬ IsSolvable G → IsSimpleGroup G

/-- A positive integer $k$ is a non-soluble group-theoretic number if and only if it is not a
soluble group-theoretic number. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNonSolubleNumber_iff_not_isSolubleNumber (k : ℕ) :
    IsNonSolubleNumber k ↔ ¬ IsSolubleNumber k := by
  simp only [IsNonSolubleNumber, IsSolubleNumber, not_forall, exists_prop]

/--
Is the set of all soluble group-theoretic numbers finite or infinite? The answer `True` means
that this set is finite and the answer `False` means that it is infinite.

A positive integer $k$ is a soluble group-theoretic number if every finite group having
exactly $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems is soluble, where an $IE_{\bar n}$-system of a finite group
$G$ is a set of all subgroups of $G$ of the same given order that contains at least one
non-normal subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.78».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ IsSolubleNumber k}.Finite := by
  sorry

/--
Is the set of all absolutely simple group-theoretic numbers finite or infinite? The answer
`True` means that this set is finite and the answer `False` means that it is infinite.

A positive integer $k$ is an absolutely simple group-theoretic number if there is at least one
simple finite group having exactly $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems and there are no non-soluble
non-simple finite groups having exactly $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.78».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ IsAbsolutelySimpleNumber k}.Finite := by
  sorry

/--
Do there exist composite, but not soluble group-theoretic numbers?

That is, is there a positive integer $k$ such that no finite simple group has exactly $k$
$IE_{\bar n}$-systems, yet some non-soluble finite group has exactly $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.78».parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ IsCompositeNumber k ∧ IsNonSolubleNumber k := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.78»

items: Subgroup 'order' is Nat.card ↥H; finite groups are quantified as (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], as in the other Kourovka files.

numIESystems is Set.ncard of the set of IE_n̄-systems in Set (Subgroup G); for finite G this ambient type is finite so ncard is the genuine count. Lemma numIESystems_eq_ncard confirms it equals the number of orders d for which G has a non-normal subgroup of order d.

'Soluble' is Mathlib's IsSolvable; 'simple' is Mathlib's IsSimpleGroup, which includes cyclic groups of prime order. These have 0 IE_n̄-systems, and every statement restricts to 0 < k, so the convention does not affect any slot (a simple group with ≥1 non-normal subgroup is non-abelian; non-soluble groups are never of prime order).
The five predicates are defined on all of ℕ; the notebook's restriction to positive integers is imposed by 0 < k in each theorem statement (documented in the module docstring).
'No non-soluble non-simple finite groups having k systems' is stated as ∀ finite G, numIESystems G = k → ¬ IsSolvable G → IsSimpleGroup G (classically equivalent to the negated existential).
Slot (iii) uses IsNonSolubleNumber (existential witness) for 'not soluble'; the API lemma isNonSolubleNumber_iff_not_isSolubleNumber proves this equals ¬ IsSolubleNumber.
'Finite or infinite?' is formalized as answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite …, so answer(True) means finite.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates formalized all three slots and are mathematically equivalent: the number of IE_n̄-systems is the number of subgroup orders d for which G has a non-normal subgroup of order d; soluble = IsSolvable, simple = IsSimpleGroup; k restricted to 0 < k; 'finite or infinite' encoded as answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite; part iii's 'not soluble' as an existential non-soluble witness. No candidate omitted anything. Differences were only stylistic: c03/c08 used theorem names (`parts.i`, `i`) not matching the slot names and c03 used awkward explicit `@` instance arguments; c02/c06/c08 defined the count directly as ncard of the set of orders; c01/c04/c05/c07 defined it literally as ncard of the set of IE-systems (sets of subgroups). c01 was chosen because it is the literal definition from the source together with a proved lemma (numIESystems_eq_ncard) that it agrees with the order-count reading in the decomposition notes, plus proved API lemmas (all-normal ⇒ 0 systems; non-soluble ↔ ¬soluble), slot-matching names, and a clean compile. My only edits: docstrings of parts i/ii now say 'finite or infinite?' and state that answer True means finite and False means infinite. Ambiguity worth noting: the source says 'exactly k' only in the first definition and 'having k' in the others; all candidates (and the final) read 'exactly k' throughout, which is the natural 'respectively' reading. The final file compiles with only the three expected 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
statement:
Any set of all subgroups of the same given order of a finite group $G$ that contains at least one non-normal subgroup is called an $IE_{\bar n}$-system of $G$. A positive integer $k$ is called a soluble (non-soluble; simple; composite; absolutely simple) group-theoretic number if every finite group having exactly $ k$ $IE_{\bar
n}$-systems is soluble (respectively, if there is at least one non-soluble finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems; if there is at least one simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems; if there are no simple finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems; if there is at least one simple finite group having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems and there are no non-soluble non-simple finite groups having $k$ $IE_{\bar n}$-systems).

Are the sets of all soluble and of all absolutely simple group-theoretic numbers finite or infinite? Do there exist composite, but not soluble group-theoretic numbers?
